sections.label: Sentencing discretion for intellectually disabled offenders
sections.summary: The Minister addresses whether the Criminal Procedure Code should be reviewed to give courts sentencing discretion and expand options for intellectually disabled offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Minister will consider reviewing the Criminal Procedure Code to (i) provide the Courts with sentencing discretion for offences mandating imprisonment and caning where the offender is intellectually disabled, and (ii) expand the sentencing options for intellectually disabled offenders, such as mandatory treatment orders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There are a number of considerations that we will need to balance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, intellectual disability occurs along a wide spectrum of severity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Persons with severe intellectual disability to the extent that they are incapable of understanding the nature and consequences of the act they had committed, are acquitted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: However, in other cases, intellectual disability may not negate the culpability of the offender.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Offences which attract mandatory imprisonment and caning are generally serious and involve violence, such as robbery and aggravated rape.

sections.label: Mandatory treatment orders and intellectual disability
sections.summary: Mandatory treatment orders are imposed for treatable mental illness contributing to an offence, but offenders with merely intellectual disability are unsuitable as their conditions were not assessed as treatable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As for Mr Louis Ng's second question, mandatory treatment orders (MTOs) are imposed when an offender is suffering from a mental illness which is treatable and which contributed to his offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: However, psychiatric assessments of offenders have found that those with merely intellectual disability are unsuitable for MTOs as their conditions were not assessed to be treatable.

sections.label: Prison resources for intellectually disabled inmates
sections.summary: A question asks whether Singapore Prison Service will give RT officers more resources to modify programmes for inmates with intellectual disability, and the review will conclude in good time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, while we are undergoing this review, will the Singapore Prison Service consider providing more resources to the RT officers so that they can modify these programmes for the inmates who are currently in there with intellectual disability?

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We will conclude the review in good time.
